evidence_quotes.two_concerns_question: we talked to a lot of people everyday and Joseph them have one of two concerns either the mover is not showing up on time or the movers might damage their items or either of those a concern for you
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer raises stairs concern: 'I know our townhome will have stairs that a lot of the stuff will be carried up' — rep acknowledges with 'Yes, mm-hmm' and brief redirect about wall protection, but does not ask 'tell me more' or dig deeper into what specifically worries them about stairs
evidence_quotes.value_days: No value days discussion; customer selected Sunday October 18th and no mention of alternative days or savings
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_then_ask: we do not require any deposit and then you will only be asked to make the payment once we completed the move... would you like to be on the schedule?

top_strength: Jeline delivered both promises (On-Time Guarantee and No Worries Damage Coverage) with full term details and built strong rapport throughout the logistics gathering and estimate explanation.
coaching_note: Step 2: when the customer raises a concern (stairs), use 'tell me more about that' and genuine silence instead of immediately pivoting to reassurance — you need two layers deep, not one concern + redirect. Step 5: Value Days was never offered despite the call being for Sunday, a non-Best-Value day. Step 6: ask 'What's still concerning you about this move?' (concerns, not questions) instead of 'Do you have any good question before I let you go?' — that throwaway closes the bookend early.
